correctness.rationale: The lower sequence is evaluated at the published branch transition, where both relevant formulas are explicit. Its gap equals p_d^*(s_d eta_d-kappa_d); an exact rearrangement isolates the leading term 3 eta_d log_2(1+(d-1)^(-2/3)) and an O((log d)/d) remainder, giving 3/(ln 2) after d^(2/3) rescaling. The published Corollary 13 supplies the matching limsup. The branch condition p_d^*<p_L,d follows asymptotically because 1-p_d^* is asymptotic to d^(-2/3), whereas 1-p_L,d is asymptotic to 4/d. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly quantifies the remaining uncertainty of a newly derived qudit entanglement-cost certificate and proves only a one-sided large-d bound. Establishing the exact constant shows that the published uniform estimate is asymptotically optimal for these two bounds and identifies the natural noise scale 1-p asymptotic to d^(-2/3) where the obstruction occurs. This directly characterizes the sharpness of the source's main unresolved qudit interval without claiming to solve the open entanglement-cost problem.
